purpose: Keep product specifications, semantic models, implementation plans, and historical handoffs understandable to future contributors and agents by assigning each a precise authority class and correcting three confirmed current-state drift claims.
scope: Documentation authority policy (docs/AUTHORITY.md), a machine-checked frontmatter authority field on docs/*.md and .claude/semantic-model/*.md, an opt-in spec-metadata convention enforced only on a small checked-in enrollment list, and the three confirmed stale claims in docs/00-design.md and .claude/semantic-model/. This track establishes maintenance rules and one automated check without rewriting repository history or retroactively enforcing anything on pre-existing files it does not explicitly enroll.
non_goals: Deleting historical handoffs, plans, or Git history.
Claiming that a plan is normative product behavior after code and specification have changed.
Creating a second prose copy of every normative requirement.
Changing plan@1's schema or adding any field to .claude/plans/*.json plan files.

Editing shared/schemas/spec@1.json or any other schema file outside this repository. That file lives in a separate repository (agent-plugins) that this spec has no authority over; the status/last_verified/owner/implementation_plan fields introduced by AC-002 are a convention tracked directly on this repo's own .claude/specs/*.json files and checked by this repo's own just lint-docs, not a schema-level constraint.

Retroactively requiring status/last_verified/owner/implementation_plan on any of the 21 .claude/specs/*.json files that exist as of this spec's authorship and are not this spec's own file. AC-002's lint-docs check only ever validates files listed in the enrollment file introduced by that criterion; a pre-existing spec that is never added to that list is never scanned and can never fail the check, this spec included no attempt to backfill them.

Making any statement about .claude/plans/ACTIVE.md's heading format a machine-checked, CI-enforced obligation. AC-001 states a link-back convention for ACTIVE.md headings as prose policy in docs/AUTHORITY.md only; no criterion in this spec wires a checker, exit code, or CI dependency to that convention, and .claude/plans/ is never scanned by lint-docs (AC-005).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A documentation authority index file exists at docs/AUTHORITY.md, listing eight document classes with their authority slug, what each covers, and which glob(s) lint-docs (AC-004) checks them against: `normative` (docs/01-spec.md and accepted .claude/specs/*/spec@1 acceptance criteria — authoritative for current required behavior), `rationale` (docs/00-design.md — explains why, not a second source of current requirements), `reference` (docs/03-polyglot-spec.md, docs/04-python-engine-spec.md, docs/05-go-engine-spec.md — subsystem/engine design references), `guide` (docs/06-publishing.md, docs/release-paradigms.md, and docs/AUTHORITY.md itself — operational how-to material; AUTHORITY.md is classified `guide` because it explains how to classify and maintain documentation rather than asserting product behavior), `historical-context` (docs/01-research-brief.md, docs/02-library-vs-moon-decision.md, and handoff documents such as .claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md — a record of past research or decisions, not current truth), `verified-current` (.claude/semantic-model/*.md — describes the implementation as verified against the current codebase), `plan-status` (.claude/plans/*.md — intended work and per-track status; not scanned by lint-docs per AC-005), and `spec-metadata` (a convention, not a frontmatter slug, applying only to files listed in the enrollment file from AC-002; not part of the docs/*.md or .claude/semantic-model/*.md frontmatter check). The index states one concrete resolution rule for conflicts: the normative source (docs/01-spec.md or an accepted spec) always wins; a non-normative document found to conflict with it receives a dated correction note in place pointing to the normative source, never a silent rewrite of its own original claims. The index also states, as prose policy only with no enforcement mechanism, that a .claude/plans/ACTIVE.md section heading marking a track DONE, SUPERSEDED, or CLOSED should reference the SPEC-id, REQ-id, or file path it implements in its body text; this is guidance for authors, not a criterion any check in this spec verifies, and .claude/plans/ is never scanned by lint-docs (AC-005).

A checked-in enrollment file exists at .claude/specs/.authority-enrolled — a plain-text file, one .claude/specs/*.json filename (basename only, no directory prefix) per line, no trailing content other than a final newline. This spec adds exactly one line to it: `SPEC-DOCUMENTATION-AUTHORITY-005.json`. Every spec@1 file whose basename appears in .claude/specs/.authority-enrolled must carry four top-level fields: status (one of draft, proposed, accepted, or superseded — the same vocabulary and field name used top-level across every spec@1 in this directory per .claude/specs/INDEX.md), last_verified_revision (the source commit SHA or revision identifier the spec was last checked against), owner_track (a track name or identifier), and implementation_plan (the workspace-relative path to its plan@1 file, e.g. .claude/plans/PLAN-006.json, or null when no plan exists yet — the normal canon-then-vector ordering permits null and it is not a violation). This spec sets its own file's fields to satisfy the check: status: proposed, last_verified_revision: the commit SHA this spec is committed in, owner_track: release-security, implementation_plan: null. No other .claude/specs/*.json file is required to carry these fields by this criterion, and none of the 21 pre-existing spec files are added to the enrollment list by this spec (see non_goals). A future spec enrolls itself by adding its own filename to .authority-enrolled as part of its own authorship — that future obligation is not itself checked or enforced by anything in this spec.

Confirmed stale current-state claims are corrected in the authoritative/current-description location. (1) docs/00-design.md line 3 currently reads exactly '**Status:** IMPLEMENTED & VERIFIED (Canonical Spec)', which is unqualified by milestone version and can be misread as covering the entire document, while line 1616 (§17 Milestones, authoritative for scope) states 'Only v0.1–v0.4 are committed. Everything past that is demand-gated per §2.2 — the'. The line is replaced with the exact literal text: '**Status:** IMPLEMENTED & VERIFIED for v0.1–v0.4 (Canonical Spec); work beyond v0.4 is demand-gated per §17/§2.2 and not scheduled.' — an exact string replacement, checkable by direct comparison, not a paraphrase. (2) .claude/semantic-model/version-flow.md lines 84-85 currently state: 'The current code has a bug here: it gates the push behind `if full.exists()`. Track B removes this gate.' This is stale: crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs's consumed_changesets loop (lines 275-285) already pushes every changeset path in cs_path to modified_paths unconditionally at line 285, outside the if full.exists() check at line 277; that if-block (lines 277-284) gates only the fs::remove_file call, since removing a nonexistent file would error. Lines 84-85 are replaced with the exact literal text: 'Track B already shipped this fix: the current code pushes every changeset path to modified_paths unconditionally (crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:285); only the fs::remove_file call is gated by `if full.exists()` (apply.rs:277-284), since removing a nonexistent file would error.' (3) .claude/semantic-model/error-taxonomy.md line 66 lists `PackageSetMatchedNothing { pattern }` as 'Defined but NEVER EMITTED — known gap.' This conflates two distinct types with the same name: `GraphError::PackageSetMatchedNothing` (crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs:294) is indeed never constructed, but `DiagnosticCode::PackageSetMatchedNothing` (crates/callisto-model/src/diagnostic.rs:162) is actively emitted as a Warning-severity Diagnostic in crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs:425 whenever a [[package-set]] rule matches zero packages. Line 66's table row is replaced with the exact literal text for its middle column: 'GraphError variant never constructed (dead code); the equivalent condition IS actively surfaced via `DiagnosticCode::PackageSetMatchedNothing` as a Warning diagnostic (walk.rs:425) — not an unqualified gap'. Each correction is validated against the referenced implementation and does not erase historical rationale.

A documentation authority check, runnable via `just lint-docs`, performs two independent scans. Scan 1 (frontmatter authority): every file matched by two globs must carry a YAML frontmatter field named `authority`, with a per-glob closed set of valid values so no glob's file can carry a slug meant for a different glob. For docs/*.md (10 files as of this spec: 00-design.md, 01-research-brief.md, 01-spec.md, 02-library-vs-moon-decision.md, 03-polyglot-spec.md, 04-python-engine-spec.md, 05-go-engine-spec.md, 06-publishing.md, release-paradigms.md, and AUTHORITY.md — AC-001 creates AUTHORITY.md inside this same glob, so its check is written against the file list including AUTHORITY.md from the start, not as a later special case), the valid values are exactly `normative`, `rationale`, `reference`, `guide`, and `historical-context` (per AC-001's mapping: 01-spec.md=normative, 00-design.md=rationale, {03-polyglot-spec.md, 04-python-engine-spec.md, 05-go-engine-spec.md}=reference, {06-publishing.md, release-paradigms.md, AUTHORITY.md}=guide, {01-research-brief.md, 02-library-vs-moon-decision.md}=historical-context). For .claude/semantic-model/*.md, the only valid value is `verified-current`. The slugs `plan-status` and `spec-metadata` are never valid within Scan 1's scope: `plan-status` belongs to .claude/plans/*.md, which this check does not scan at all (AC-005); `spec-metadata` names a convention checked by Scan 2, not a frontmatter value. A docs/*.md or .claude/semantic-model/*.md file carrying either slug is a violation under Scan 1's `invalid authority value` category (AC-006), same as any other value outside its glob's closed set. Scan 2 (spec metadata): for every filename listed in .claude/specs/.authority-enrolled (AC-002), the corresponding .claude/specs/<filename> is checked for status, last_verified_revision, and owner_track as present non-empty top-level JSON keys (implementation_plan is optional and may be null or absent), and that status's value is one of draft, proposed, accepted, or superseded. No .claude/specs/*.json file outside the enrollment list is read by Scan 2. On success — every file matched by Scan 1's two globs carries a present, valid-for-its-glob authority field, and every enrolled spec file passes Scan 2 — `just lint-docs` exits 0 and prints a single summary line to stdout (e.g. `lint-docs: N files checked, 0 violations`). On failure — any Scan 1 file has the field missing, malformed, or invalid for its glob, or any Scan 2 enrolled file is missing a required field or has an invalid status value (see AC-006 for the distinct failure categories) — it exits 1, lists every offending file's path with one line per violation on stdout, and does not automatically rewrite any file's content. `just lint-docs` is defined as its own Justfile recipe, following the existing pattern of `doc-check` (Justfile:71) rather than being merged into `lint` (whose own comment scopes it to the workspace Clippy invocation), and is added as a dependency of both the `ci` and `ci-fast` recipes alongside `doc-check` (Justfile:159, Justfile:167).

`just lint-docs` (both scans defined in AC-004) never reads, scans, or flags any file under .claude/plans/ — including .claude/plans/ACTIVE.md and .claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md — for the authority field or any other check; a plan or handoff document missing frontmatter, or any heading in ACTIVE.md missing a link-back reference, never appears in lint-docs's violation report and never affects its exit code. This is independent of, and does not need to reconcile with, the prose-only convention AC-001 states for ACTIVE.md headings — that convention has no checker.

`just lint-docs` treats the following as distinct failure categories, each labeled explicitly in its violation report rather than collapsed into a single generic message: (1) `missing authority field` — a docs/*.md or .claude/semantic-model/*.md file (Scan 1) with no frontmatter block or a frontmatter block lacking the `authority` key; (2) `malformed frontmatter` — a Scan 1 file whose frontmatter block is present but is not parseable YAML; (3) `invalid authority value: <value>` — a Scan 1 file whose `authority` value is outside the closed set valid for that file's glob (AC-004), including the case where a docs/*.md or .claude/semantic-model/*.md file carries `plan-status` or `spec-metadata`; (4) `missing spec-metadata field: <field>` — an enrolled spec file (Scan 2, AC-002) missing status, last_verified_revision, or owner_track; (5) `invalid spec-metadata status: <value>` — an enrolled spec file whose status value is not one of draft, proposed, accepted, or superseded. Each violation line names the specific file and the specific category from this list; no category is ever reported using another category's label.
